demos.title: Tony Bony's Rock Kitchen
demos.blurb: Cook up rocks with Tony! Blend, squish, and melt your way around the rock cycle.
demos.about: Kids pull rocks from the cabinet and run them through kitchen machines like the Weather Blender to see what they turn into. Tony fills orders, cheers discoveries, and tells a pun for every occasion. Built for grades 1–3 playing with a parent.

demos.title: Tony Bony's Rock Cycle Kitchen
demos.blurb: The older-grades kitchen: rock-cycle quests, machines, and the real names for every step.
demos.about: The same kitchen for older students, with the real vocabulary: weathering, compaction, metamorphism, and melting. Quest mode walks a rock all the way around the cycle, one machine at a time.

demos.title: What's Earth Made Of?
demos.blurb: Click through Earth's layers with Tony to see which elements make up the core, mantle, crust, oceans, air, and life.
demos.about: A click-to-zoom ring chart of Earth sized by weight. Start with the whole planet, then open the inner and outer core, the mantle, the crust, the oceans, the air, and living things to see their elements. Click any element to see where all of Earth's supply of it is (almost all the iron is in the core). Switch to By atoms to watch light hydrogen jump from tiny to huge in water and living things. Tony gives a fact and a pun for every stop.

demos.title: Atom Builder
demos.blurb: Add protons, neutrons, and electrons and watch the element change.
demos.about: Click to add or remove protons, neutrons, and electrons. The element card updates live with its name, mass number, and charge, so students see that the proton count decides which element it is.

demos.title: Atom Builder 2.0
demos.blurb: Build atoms, highlight valence electrons, then switch to reaction mode.
demos.about: Everything in Atom Builder plus electron shells, a valence-electron highlight, and a reaction mode for exploring how atoms combine.

demos.title: Beta Decay Lab
demos.blurb: Step through a neutron turning into a proton, one vertex at a time.
demos.about: A step-by-step walkthrough of beta decay. Students advance through each moment as a neutron becomes a proton, and the lab tracks charge and particle counts so they can check that everything balances.

demos.title: Tony Bony's Bomb Squad
demos.blurb: Balance the chemical equation before the timer hits zero to disarm the bomb!
demos.about: Drag number and element tiles into the equation until the atoms match on both sides. Ten levels build from counting atoms (big number × little number) to real class demos: electrolysis, rust, elephant toothpaste, burning methane, lampblack, baking soda and vinegar, and untarnishing silver. Tony walks students through the first two levels, and a Practice mode turns the timer off.

demos.title: Pane Fracture Lab
demos.blurb: Pick a pane and an impactor, then see how annealed and tempered glass crack differently.
demos.about: Choose a glass pane (annealed or tempered), an impactor, and a strike strength, then hit it. Annealed glass breaks into long shards, while tempered glass shatters into small cubes. Great for talking about stored stress and safety glass.

demos.title: Glass Breaking Simulator (original)
demos.blurb: The first-try glass simulator, kept for comparison with Pane Fracture Lab.
demos.about: The first version of the glass simulator, left as it was (apart from an animation fix) so students can compare it with Pane Fracture Lab and see how a model improves when you test it.

demos.title: O'Neill Cylinder Simulator
demos.blurb: Spin up a space habitat and see how rotation makes artificial gravity.
demos.about: A 3D model of a rotating space habitat. Change its size and spin rate and watch the 'gravity' felt on the inside surface change. Throw a ball to see why things move strangely inside a spinning world.

demos.title: Space-time Block
demos.blurb: Stack the frames of a video into a 3D block to see motion as a shape in space and time.
demos.about: Stack a video's frames into a 3D block so that time becomes a direction you can see. Moving objects trace out tubes and curves through the block, which turns motion into a shape.

demos.title: Slice: 3D & 4D Cross-Sections
demos.blurb: Slice shapes with a plane to see their cross-sections, then try it on 4D shapes.
demos.about: Drop in spheres, cubes, cones, a torus (even a hand), then tilt and slide a cutting plane to watch the 2D slice change. Then step up a dimension: slide a 3D 'hyperplane' through a tesseract, hypersphere, 5-cell, or 24-cell and see the 3D shapes that appear, grow, and morph.

demos.title: How Machines Learn: Pixel Trainer
demos.blurb: Train a tiny model by grading its guesses, then flip the rubric and watch what it learned.
demos.about: Students train a tiny model by grading its guesses, then test it. Flip the rubric and the score drops, because the model learned the old rule. Retrain and it recovers. A hands-on look at how training shapes behavior.

demos.title: Pixel Trainer: Deep Network
demos.blurb: The same pixel task with two hidden layers and real backpropagation you can watch.
demos.about: A bigger network trains on the same brightest-pixel task. Watch signals flow forward and weight changes flash backward after each grade, hover any node to see its arithmetic, and step through 'Why this guess?' and 'What did backprop change?' Then hit 'Train until 90%' to see why extra layers beat the one-layer ceiling.

demos.title: Tony's Picker
demos.blurb: Spin the wheel and let Tony pick who's next. Saves your class lists.
demos.about: A spinning name wheel for calling on students, with Tony as host. It keeps lists for several classes and can remove names as they're picked, so everyone gets a turn.
